To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

gender-based violence and inequity are significant contributors to the social production of disease and illness in the Peruvian amazon and that these inequities are compounded by intersecting social disadvantages such as poverty, ethnicity and geography.
gender inequities in Peru’s Amazon are shaped by the intersection of multiple social disadvantages that result in health inequities and structural violence.

gender inequities are reproduced through a complex set of interrelated social processes and structural violence, which in turn contribute to health inequities and health outcomes in the Peruvian Amazons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social construction of health and disease and its relationship to the social construction of gender.
the intersectionality of gender, ethnicity, class and geographical location in shaping gender and health inequalitites.
the intersection of gender, health, and structural violence in the Amazon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gendered social order in Amazonian Peru is characterized by a high degree of gender inequality that is exacerbated by other social inequities, and that gender inequities and other social inequity intersect to produce health inequity.
gender is a social institution which interacts with and intersects with other social inequalities to reproduce gender-based health inequities and health disparities.

gender-based violence, discrimination, and inequitable access to healthcare are significant factors in the production of poor health outcomes in the Peruvian Amazons, and that a structural violence approach provides a framework to understand the complex and interrelated social forces that contribute to these inequities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gendered nature of social inequalities and health inequity in the Peruvian lowlands is shaped by the intersection of gender and structural violence.

gender-based inequities in the Peruvian context are not simply a matter of gender but rather a complex intersection of gender, class and ethnicity, and are thus best understood through an intersectional lens.
the gender-based violence, discrimination and marginalization that women experience in Amazonian Peru is not simply an individual or interpersonal issue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gender is not a single axis of inequality, but is rather one among many social determinants of inequities in access to healthcare and poor health outcomes.
gender-based inequalities are not only a result of individual-level factors, but are also a result of structural forces and social inequities.
gender inequity is a key determinant of health in the Peruvian lowlands and must be addressed in order to improve the health of Amazonian women.
